target_customer: CEOs, CFOs, managers and office managers at small businesses who send monthly PDF bills to an accountant
problem: Small businesses lose time every month logging into many vendor portals (Uber, Amazon, AWS, ad platforms, utilities) to download PDF bills for their accountant.
business_model: SMB software subscription (desktop app that fetches bills into Dropbox); pricing not found
product_category: Accounting automation, bill and invoice retrieval

founders.name: Michael Ohana
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CEO and gives no background. No bio source found.

founders.name: Aric Lasry
previous_startups: Daigest (co-founder, per the YC profile link; outcome not researched)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CTO and notes the Daigest affiliation. No education or employer source found.

exit.reason: Not stated by the company; YC and Dealroom list it as inactive or closed with no announcement found.

competitors.name: Hubdoc
competitors.what: Canadian document capture service for accountants that integrated with Xero and collected bills and statements for bookkeepers
competitors.traction_then: Named a Xero App Partner of the Year at Xerocon 2016
competitors.funding_then: Seed round of US$4.85M announced in June 2017, after the batch; amount before that not found

technical_complexity.rationale: A desktop app had to log in to many vendor portals with credentials kept in the local keychain and scrape PDFs reliably. Each portal needed its own connector and portals change often, which is a maintenance burden for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Scraping connectors can be copied, there was no network effect, and customers could switch easily. Established accounting capture tools could add the same feature.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Xero acquired Hubdoc in August 2018, which absorbed the closest wedge into a major accounting platform. Whether Hellobill was affected is not documented.

market_need_then: The YC description frames monthly bill collection as a tedious accounting chore for small businesses. The launch copy lists common vendors and says users refocus on their business. No independent demand data from 2016 was found.

branding.domain_note: Used hellobill.io, not a .com; the .io domain now returns errors (HTTP 503 on fetch).

identity.logo: Not described by any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly and plain: 'Say hi to Hellobill' and 'Imagine if all your PDF bills could be automatically downloaded' in the YC description.

brand_strength.rationale: No press, community, merch or brand coverage found beyond directory listings. A two person company with a generic compound name similar to HelloFax and other Hello brands.

outcome_analysis: Hellobill was a two person Summer 2016 company selling a desktop app that downloaded online PDF bills for accountants. No funding, shutdown announcement or post-mortem was found, so the cause of its inactive status is not public and failure factors are left empty. The product wedge was close to what Hubdoc and Receipt Bank already offered, and Xero bought Hubdoc in 2018, but no source ties that to Hellobill's end.
notes: Company website hellobill.io returned HTTP 503 when fetched, so treated as dead or unreachable. Seedtable says no funding rounds recorded; this is not evidence of zero funding. YC does not give founding date beyond the batch. Searches for the cause of closure (outcome search) returned only the YC and Dealroom status and unrelated shutdowns (Bench, Botkeeper). Hubdoc is listed on the strength of its Xerocon 2016 award coverage; its auto-fetch features in 2016 are not confirmed by a dated source.
